correctness.rationale: For B e_j=(log(j+e))^-1 e_(j-1) on complex l^p (1<=p<infty) or c0, decreasing weights imply exact ||B^k||=P_k=exp(-F(k)); F(k)/k->infinity gives compactness and spectral radius zero. Maximizing k log t-F(k)-a k/log(k+e) places log k=t-a+o(1) and yields H_a(t)~e^(t-a)/t, by summation/integration of loglog and logarithmic-integral residual. Max-term versus sum has at most O(t) logarithmic overhead using cut K=e^(2t), negligible on this scale. Neumann expansion gives the uniform-in-argument global upper, and the e_k zeroth coordinate lower gives log||R||~e^t/t. For x^a_j=e^(-a j/log(j+e)), positive real lambda gives lower via zeroth output and l^p/c0 tails give matching upper, hence exponent e^-a. e0 gives 0, y_j=e^(-j/log^2(j+e)) gives 1, and the universal norm bounds confine exponents to [0,1]. The bundled finite saddle diagnostic was read; the asymptotic follows from the infinite saddle argument rather than finite sampled t.
